correctness.rationale: The multiplication rule e_i e_j=e_(2j-i mod 4) gives intrinsic two-dimensional right annihilator W=span(e0-e2,e1-e3). Every automorphism preserves W and has invertible block A,D. For characteristic unequal to two, independent quotient characters epsilon,delta force epsilon A=epsilon, delta A=+/- delta, zero shear C, and diagonal/antidiagonal D: exactly (K^*)^2 semidirect C2. In characteristic two, multiplication in coordinates is (u,w)(v,z)=(lambda(v)u,lambda(v)w+(u0v1,u1v0)); coefficient comparison forces A=D=I or simultaneous swap while C is arbitrary: M2(K)^+ semidirect C2. Both necessity and sufficiency are proved and unique blocks counted. Exhaustive original multiplication-table checks of 576 W-preserving invertible matrices over F2 (32 automorphisms) and 186624 over F3 (8 automorphisms) match. The finite checks are not substituted for the arbitrary-field proof.

originality.rationale: The 2020/2022 integral-coefficient R4 theorem gives an abstract eight-element group but does not classify field-coefficient automorphisms, much less the characteristic-two 2q^4 family. The 2026 paper states the higher-even integral problem and derives only an injective representation for even dihedral algebras over domains of characteristic not two. Direct comparison of domains and normal forms shows neither published result implies the complete two-branch field formula. Focused published-record and primary-literature searches did not find an identical field classification. Historical priority is qualified: earlier unindexed quandle-algebra calculations could exist.
residual_risks: Unindexed older computations might state the same field classification under rack/quandle ring or a closely equivalent nonassociative-algebra normal form.
The theorem is narrow to R4; it does not resolve the general higher-even integral classification problem.

value.rationale: Automorphism groups of even dihedral quandle algebras are a natural current classification problem (Problem 4.14 of arXiv:2608.01550). This is the smallest nontrivial even case and yields a complete all-field group structure, with a nonobvious characteristic-two transition from a two-parameter multiplicative torus to a four-parameter additive shear group. It makes exact predictions in all finite fields and explains their origin structurally. It is not a mere finite sample, renaming, or a restatement of known integral automorphisms, and the limitations on higher even orders are explicit.
